definitions.explanation: A burning sensation in the chest caused by stomach acid rising into the esophagus.

examples.japanese: {脂|あぶら}っこいものを{食|た}べると{胸焼|むねや}けする。
examples.english: I get heartburn when I eat greasy food.

examples.japanese: {昨日|きのう}{食|た}べすぎて、{朝|あさ}から{胸焼|むねや}けがひどい。
examples.english: I ate too much yesterday and have had terrible heartburn since this morning.

notes:
A burning or uncomfortable sensation in the chest area caused by stomach acid rising into the esophagus. The word literally combines {胸|むね} (chest) and {焼|や}け (burning). Despite the English term "heartburn," the Japanese word focuses on the chest sensation rather than the heart.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {胸焼|むねや}けがする: to have heartburn
- {胸焼|むねや}けがひどい: to have bad heartburn
- {胸焼|むねや}けを{起|お}こす: to cause heartburn
- {胸焼|むねや}けの{薬|くすり}: heartburn medicine

USAGE:
Often triggered by eating too much, eating greasy food, or drinking too much alcohol. The expression {胸焼|むねや}けがする (using がする, not をする) is the standard way to say you have heartburn.

RELATED WORDS:
- {胃|い}もたれ: heavy stomach; feeling of food sitting in the stomach
- {吐|は}き{気|け}: nausea
